messages.content:
You check what a company's executives said on an earnings call against the company's annual report (Form 10-K), as a careful analyst would. You get one claim from the call and a few numbered 10-K passages found by search. For each passage, decide how it bears on the claim:

- contradiction: both are about the same thing (the same measure, scope and period, or the same fact about the company) and they can't both be true: figures that differ by more than rounding, opposite directions, or one saying something is so and the other that it isn't.
- consistent: the passage states the same thing, or something that agrees with it.
- unrelated: the passage doesn't speak to what the claim states, or covers a different period, segment or measure.

Not contradictions:
- A forecast, target or plan, and a different actual result for that period or a later, revised target. Plans change; that's news, not a contradiction.
- A risk the 10-K says could happen, and executives sounding confident on the call.
- Figures for different periods or scopes: a quarter and the full year, one segment and the whole company, adjusted (non-GAAP) and reported figures.
- Rounding, different wording, or one side giving more detail.
Flag a contradiction only when an analyst shown the two quotes side by side would agree they can't both be true.

The call quote is what was said; the claim sentence summarizes it to help you read it. The transcript is a machine transcription, so a misspelled name is still the same name.

For each passage, give a short reason first (what each side says), then the verdict, and filing_quote: the clause of the passage the verdict rests on, copied exactly, character for character, at most about 40 words. Leave filing_quote empty when the passage is unrelated.

Company: CONOCOPHILLIPS

On the Q3 2020 earnings call, Matt Fox said (metric):
Quote: "we'd be at the top end in that range."
Claim: ConocoPhillips would be at the top end of the CFO range if distributions are similar to this year.

10-K passages:

[F1] 10-K for fiscal 2020, filed 2021-02-16 · Item 7. MANAGEMENT’S DISCUSSION AND ANALYSIS OF FINANCIAL CONDITION AND RESULTS OF OPERATIONS
Key Operating and Financial Summary

Significant items during 2020 and recent announcements included the following:

● Enhanced both our portfolio and financial framework through the acquisition of Concho in an all-stock transaction, as well as purchasing bolt-on acreage in Canada and Lower 48.

● Full-year production, excluding Libya, of 1,118 MBOED; curtailed approximately 80 MBOED during the year.

● Cash provided by operating activities was $4.8 billion.

● Generated $1.3 billion in disposition proceeds from non-core asset sales.

● Distributed $1.8 billion in dividends and repurchased $0.9 billion of shares.

● Ended the year with cash and cash equivalents totaling $3.0 billion and short-term investments of $3.6 billion, equaling $6.6 billion in ending cash and cash equivalents and short-term investments.

● Announced two significant discoveries in Norway and achieved first production at Tor II; continued appraisal drilling and started up first pads and related infrastructure in Montney.

● Adopted a Paris-aligned climate risk framework with ambition to achieve net -zero operated emissions by 2050 as part of our commitment to ESG excellence.

● Recognized impairments of proved and unproved properties totaling $1.3 billion after-tax.

[F2] 10-K for fiscal 2020, filed 2021-02-16 · Item 7. MANAGEMENT’S DISCUSSION AND ANALYSIS OF FINANCIAL CONDITION AND RESULTS OF OPERATIONS
Net Income (Loss) Attributable to ConocoPhillips

(millions of dollars) | $(1,122) | 436 | 1,747

[F3] 10-K for fiscal 2020, filed 2021-02-16 · Item 7. MANAGEMENT’S DISCUSSION AND ANALYSIS OF FINANCIAL CONDITION AND RESULTS OF OPERATIONS › Overview
In October 2020, we announced an increase to our quarterly dividend from $0.42 per share to $0.43 per share and resumed share repurchases before suspending our share repurchase program upon entry into our definitive agreement to acquire Concho. We resumed shares repurchases in February 2021 after completion of our Concho acquisition. We ended the year with over $12 billion of liquidity, comprised of $3.0 billion in cash and cash equivalents, $3.6 billion in short-term investments, and available borrowings under our credit facility of $5.7 billion.

Our expectation is that commodity prices will remain cyclical and volatile, and a successful business strategy in the E&P industry must be resilient in lower price environments, at the same time retaining upside during periods of higher prices. While we are not impervious to current market conditions, we believe our decisive actions over the last several years of focusing on free cash flow generation, high-grading our asset base, lowering the cost of supply of our investment resource portfolio, and strengthening our balance sheet have put us in a strong relative position compared to our independent E&P peers. We remain committed to the core principles of our value proposition, namely, free cash flow generation, a strong balance sheet, commitment to differential returns of and on capital, and ESG leadership.

reason.description: What each side says, and why that's the verdict

filing_quote.description: Exact text from the passage the verdict rests on; empty if unrelated
